title: Edmonton’s Connor McDavid wins fifth Ted Lindsay Award as league’s most outstanding player
content:
Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid is this year’s recipient of the Ted Lindsay Award, awarded to the NHL’s most outstanding player as voted by the National Hockey League Players’ Association. McDavid bested fellow finalists Macklin Celebrini of the San Jose Sharks and reigning winner Nikita Kucherov of the Tampa Bay Lightning.

This win has McDavid in rarefied air. McDavid and Hall of Famer Wayne Gretzky are the only five-time Ted Lindsay Award winners in NHL history.

“This award, coming from the guys that you play against every single night and battle against every single night,” McDavid said. “And to have them recognize me (with) an award like this, that means so much.”

This is also McDavid’s first Ted Lindsay Award win since 2023. That year was also the last time McDavid won the Hart Trophy as the league’s most valuable player, and he is hoping to win the trophy for a fourth time. McDavid is a finalist for this season’s award alongside Kucherov and Colorado Avalanche forward Nathan MacKinnon.

In line with the NHL’s recent surprise announcements, McDavid was presented with the trophy by his parents while he was at a golf course with friends and family.

“I was texting my buddies mid-round, and they weren’t texting me back,” McDavid said. “I thought that was a little bit odd. Such a special way to do it, with family here, friends, hometown buddies that I don’t get to spend too much time with. It definitely means a lot.”

McDavid recorded 48 goals and 138 points in 82 games with the Oilers in 2025-26, registering his sixth consecutive 100-point season and his sixth Art Ross Trophy, the annual award presented to the league’s points leader. McDavid also led the NHL with 90 assists, the second-highest single-season total in his 11-year career. McDavid is tied with Gordie Howe and Mario Lemieux for the second-most Art Ross Trophy wins in league history. Gretzky is the all-time leader with 10 Art Ross trophies.

The Oilers’ captain also led the NHL in power-play points (54) this season and tied with Celebrini for the third-most even-strength points (82). McDavid finished third in the Maurice Richard Trophy race for most goals, trailing MacKinnon and the Montreal Canadiens’ Cole Caufield. McDavid reached the career 1,200-point mark this past regular season, becoming the third-fastest player to accomplish the feat. Only Gretzky and Lemieux reached 1,200 points in fewer games.

McDavid helped the Oilers make the playoffs for a seventh consecutive season, with the team finishing second in the Pacific Division.
